hook: This plane's whole nose swings open.
narration: This plane's whole nose swings open, and inside was a heat shield that had been to the Moon and back.
NASA's Super Guppy is a one-of-a-kind, turboprop-powered cargo plane.
On November sixth, 2023, it touched down in Huntsville, Alabama.
Its cargo was the heat shield that protected Orion's crew module on the Artemis One flight.
The nose is hinged and can open up to a hundred and ten degrees, so cargo too big for any side door goes straight in the front.
The shield rode inside a giant white crate. [short pause]
outcome: The Super Guppy delivered the heat shield to Huntsville, for the trip to NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center.
title: This plane's whole nose opens
description:
NASA's Super Guppy cargo plane arrived in Huntsville, Alabama, on Nov. 6, 2023, carrying the heat shield that protected Orion's crew module during Artemis I, bound for NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center.

facts.claim: Super Guppy arrived in Alabama Nov 6 2023 with Orion's Artemis I heat shield
facts.source_quote: NASA's Super Guppy arrives in Alabama on Nov. 6, 2023, carrying the heat shield that protected Orion’s crew module during its flight on Artemis I.

facts.claim: One-of-a-kind turboprop, delivered to Huntsville for Marshall
facts.source_quote: The one-of-a-kind, turboprop-powered aircraft ferried the heat shield from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida to Huntsville International Airport for transport to the agency’s Marshall Space Flight Center.

facts.claim: Hinged nose opens up to 110 degrees for front loading
facts.source_quote: The Super Guppy is capable of hauling heavy, large cargo, and its unique, hinged nose can open up to 110 degrees, allowing NASA teams to load and unload that heavy, bulky cargo from the front of the aircraft.
